plain_english: This clause says the written contract is the complete and final agreement between you and the client; anything said before or outside the contract doesn’t count.
what_it_means_for_you: You can’t rely on any oral promises or side‑notes that aren’t written in the contract.
risk_reasons: It limits reliance on any prior or informal understandings, which could be a disadvantage if you expected extra benefits not captured in writing.
questions_to_ask: Are there any verbal promises or side agreements that you need to get written into the contract?
How will the client’s amendment right in clause (b) interact with this ‘entire agreement’ provision?
evidence_quote: This Agreement constitutes the entire agreement between the parties.
